faq: Where does the price data come from?
From your own eBay sales and from sold listings that anyone can see on eBay. We do not scrape other sites or buy data lists. We note where the sample is small, so you can weigh it.
Do you change prices without asking?
No. You approve each change list first. After that we update the listings in bulk and record the old prices in a sheet, so you can go back if you wish.
How do Best Offer rules work?
You choose a lowest price you will accept and a price below which offers are declined automatically. We calculate those from your costs, set them on each listing and test a couple of offers.
Can you make a sale on eBay?
Yes, using eBay's markdown manager and promotions in your account, with real start and end dates. We do not show invented original prices to make an offer look larger.
desc:
An eBay pricing review and Best Offer settings project shows what your items really earn after fees and sets rules that protect your margin. Ecom Swift LLC compares sold prices, works out your profit per item and applies changes only after you approve them.

## Why does eBay pricing need more than a guess?

eBay pricing needs data because the listed price is only part of the picture. After the sale you pay selling fees, possibly ad fees, and the cost of postage and packing. An item that looks profitable can leave very little once those costs are counted, and an item priced too low can sell fast and still lose money.

The opposite mistake is just as common. A price set far above what buyers pay for the same item can sit unsold for months, tying up stock and cash.

## How price and offer rules shape results

Price is one of the strongest signals a buyer weighs, next to condition and shipping cost. Matching your price to what similar items actually sold for, not just what sellers are asking, makes the item competitive without giving margin away.

Best Offer adds a second lever. Many buyers like to negotiate, and clear rules let you respond without effort: accept offers above a floor, decline offers below it and let the rest wait. Rules keep your decisions consistent and spare you from answering every offer by hand. Demand and competition still affect the outcome, and we cannot control them.

## What a sound pricing review includes

- Your own recent sales for each item, used as the first reference.
- Public sold listings for similar items, to show what buyers have paid.
- A profit figure that subtracts eBay fees, ad fees, postage and packing.
- Your cost of goods, where you share it with us.
- Suggested price changes, with a reason beside each.
- Best Offer auto-accept and auto-decline thresholds for each listing.
- Plans for sale events using eBay's own markdown tools.
- Multi-buy and volume offers, where they suit the items.
- A reusable pricing sheet, so you can repeat the method yourself.

## What we do

We gather your sales history and compare it with public sold listings for similar items. Then we calculate what you keep after fees and shipping, and list every item where the price looks too low, too high or unprofitable. You see this as a clear sheet before anything changes.

When you approve, we apply the price changes and set Best Offer rules. The Basic package checks a small group of top items. The Standard package adds more items, Best Offer rules, a planned sale event and the reusable sheet. The Premium package covers a large range, plans several events across the year, adds multi-buy and volume offers and produces a seasonal price calendar.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Share your real cost per item so profit figures are honest.
- Set an offer floor that you would be happy to accept.
- Compare against items sold, not only items listed.
- Review prices again after a busy season.
- Keep a record of every price change and its date.

**Avoid:**
- Matching the lowest price on the page without checking condition.
- Forgetting postage and fees when you judge a price.
- Running a sale on items that already have thin margins.
- Setting auto-accept so low that it creates losses.
- Changing many prices at once with no record to compare.

## Who this is for

This service suits a seller who suspects some items lose money but cannot tell which. It suits a shop owner with many offers arriving each week, and a seller planning a seasonal sale who wants the numbers checked first.

## What we need from you

Send your cost of goods if you can, tell us your lowest acceptable margin and point out any items you never want discounted. Tell us how you handle postage so we can count it correctly. We never ask for your password. We work through the access eBay allows for your account, and no price changes are made until you say yes.
